title: How a class says where it lives
summary: Class: ::annotate class K table "schema.table" key "col" [generate "max"]. Attribute annotations: column C (a value in the class's table); column C table T (a value in extension table T sharing the class's key: a one-to-one split); one K column C (a reference to one K whose key column C here holds); many K column C (the K objects whose column C holds this one's key); many K link L from F to T (the K objects through link table L, F holding this key and T the K's); owned "yes"/"no" on a many (default: a column many is owned, a link many is shared; a one cannot be owned). schema is the name the store attached a database under. Example in packages/oorexx_oodialog_designer_v0.9/data/People.cls (Person, Address, Note, Company).
invariants: Owned parts are deleted with the object and when taken out of the collection; shared parts lose only their link row or their reference (which must then allow NULL).
The target class of a part is found beside the mapped class (its package), else in the caller's package.
Annotations are read by reflection (cls~annotation(k), method~annotations); an attribute's annotations sit on its getter and setter.
